sections.heading: From Features to Feelings
sections.body: Traditional requirements list features and acceptance criteria. Vibe-driven requirements add a layer of feeling. We describe the emotional arc of a flow—confidence rising, confusion fading, momentum building—and then translate the arc into measurable signals. Instead of 'user can upload a file', we write 'user sees progress within 150ms, can undo within 5s, and receives a readable summary on completion'.

sections.heading: Story Beats
sections.body: A beat is a small moment where something meaningful happens. We write beats as short lines: 'Tap upload → progress appears', 'Drop fails → friendly repair path suggests try again', 'Upload completes → CTA moves attention to next step'. Beats help designers and engineers agree on a cadence before building screens.

sections.heading: Framing Constraints
sections.body: We articulate constraints as part of the vibe: 'No blocking dialogs for low-risk actions', 'Maximum two visual states during upload', 'No irreversible actions without preview'. Constraints act as guardrails. They prevent regressions when pressure mounts and create an environment where the intended vibe persists.

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria with Vibes
sections.body: Acceptance criteria evolve from assertions to experiential checks. We include time budgets for feedback, language tone guidelines, and diversity checks for accessibility. A criterion might say: 'On slow networks, a skeleton loads within 100ms and a message explains degraded mode in simple language.' We pair automated tests with manual vibe checks during review.

sections.heading: Prioritizing Feels
sections.body: When schedule pressure rises, teams cut scope. Vibe-driven requirements help cut wisely: we keep moments that sustain confidence and remove decorative options that don’t improve outcomes. For example, we might reduce advanced filters but preserve the undo path and typed-in state retention.

sections.heading: Non-Goals that Prevent Drift
sections.body: We state what we will not do: 'No infinite loading spinners without contextual messaging', 'No surprise navigation', 'No growth tactics that erode trust'. Non-goals protect the vibe from well-intentioned but harmful additions.

sections.heading: Workshops
sections.body: Gather the team for a vibe workshop. Read a first-run story and mark beats. Ask: where might trust be lost? Identify quick signals that reinforce confidence. Convert insights to one-page vibe requirements that live alongside the technical spec. Revisit after the first prototype to adjust time budgets and copy.

sections.heading: Exercises
sections.body: Write a vibe requirement for a login flow: optimistic field validation, gentle error copy, and a clear repair path for password reset. Set explicit time budgets for feedback and screen transitions. Define non-goals to prevent modal overuse.
